en: Thus have I heard: the Mūlapariyāya Sutta, the First Discourse of the Majjhima Nikāya.
On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Ukkaṭṭhā in the Subhaga Grove at the foot of a royal sāla tree.
There the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus!”
“Venerable Sir,” those bhikkhus replied to the Blessed One.
The Blessed One said this:
“Bhikkhus, I will teach you the exposition on the root of all phenomena.”
“Listen to that and attend closely; I shall speak.
“Yes, venerable sir,” those bhikkhus replied to the Blessed One.
The Blessed One said this:

“Here, monks, an uninstructed worldling—who has no regard for the noble ones, is unskilled in the Dhamma of the noble ones, and undisciplined in the Dhamma of the noble ones; who has no regard for true persons, is unskilled in the Dhamma of true persons, and undisciplined in the Dhamma of true persons—perceives earth as earth.
Having perceived earth as earth, he conceives of earth, he conceives himself in earth, he conceives himself apart from earth, he conceives ‘earth is mine,’ and he delights in earth.
For what reason?
Because it has not been fully understood, I say.
One perceives water as water.
Having perceived water as water, one conceives of water, one conceives in water, one conceives from water, one conceives "water is mine," and one delights in water.
For what reason?
Because it has not been fully understood by him, I say.
One perceives fire as fire.
Having perceived fire as fire, one conceives of fire, one conceives in fire, one conceives from fire, one conceives "fire is mine," and one delights in fire.
For what reason?
‘It is not fully understood by him,’ I say.
One perceives wind as wind;
having perceived wind as wind, one conceives of wind, conceives in wind, conceives from wind, conceives ‘wind is mine,’ and delights in wind.
And why is that? Because I say that it has not been fully understood by him.
He perceives beings as beings.

Having perceived what has come to be as it truly is, one conceives of what has come to be, one conceives in relation to what has come to be, one conceives from what has come to be, one conceives, "What has come to be is mine," and one delights in what has come to be.
For what reason?
Because it has not been fully understood by him, I say.
One perceives as "deity" what is a deity;
having perceived it as a deity, one conceives of deities, conceives oneself among deities, conceives oneself as a deity, conceives "deities are mine," and delights in deities.
For what reason?
‘That has not been fully understood by him,’ I say.
He perceives Pajāpati as Pajāpati;
having perceived Pajāpati as Pajāpati, he conceives Pajāpati, he conceives in Pajāpati, he conceives from Pajāpati, he conceives ‘Pajāpati is mine,’ and he delights in Pajāpati.
For what reason?
Because it has not been fully understood by him, I say.
He perceives the divine as divine.

Having perceived the Brahmā as Brahmā, one conceives of the Brahmā; one conceives oneself as being the Brahmā; one conceives [something] from the Brahmā; one conceives "the Brahmā is mine"; one delights in the Brahmā. For what reason?
"Because it has not been fully understood by him," I say.
One perceives the Ābhassara beings as Ābhassara beings;

having perceived the Ābhassara beings as Ābhassara beings, one conceives of the Ābhassara beings, conceives in the Ābhassara beings, conceives "from" the Ābhassara beings, conceives "the Ābhassara beings are mine," and delights in the Ābhassara beings.
For what reason?
“I say that this has not been fully understood by him.
He perceives the Subhakinhā devas as Subhakinhā;

having perceived the Subhakinhā devas as Subhakinhā, he conceives [a notion] of the Subhakinhā, he conceives among the Subhakinhā, he conceives from the Subhakinhā, he conceives ‘the Subhakinhā are mine,’ and he delights in the Subhakinhā.”
And why is that? Because I say that it has not been fully understood by him.
He perceives the Vehapphala realm as the Vehapphala realm.

Perceiving the Vehapphala [deities] as the Vehapphala, one conceives of the Vehapphala, conceives in the Vehapphala, conceives from the Vehapphala, conceives "the Vehapphala is mine," and delights in the Vehapphala.
For what reason?
I say it is because they have not fully understood them.
One who is overcome conceives of the conqueror;

having conceived of the conqueror, one imagines oneself as the conqueror, imagines oneself within the conqueror, imagines oneself as being overcome, imagines "the conqueror is mine," and delights in the conqueror.
For what reason?
‘It is not fully understood by him,’ I say.
One perceives the base of infinite space as the base of infinite space;
having perceived the base of infinite space as the base of infinite space, one conceives of the base of infinite space, [and clings] to the base of infinite space.
One conceives; one conceives from the base of infinite space; one conceives, "The base of infinite space is mine"; one delights in the base of infinite space.
For what reason?
Because it has not been fully understood by him, I say.
One perceives the base of infinite consciousness as the base of infinite consciousness;
having perceived the base of infinite consciousness as the base of infinite consciousness, one conceives of the base of infinite consciousness, conceives in the base of infinite consciousness,
conceives from the base of infinite consciousness, conceives "the base of infinite consciousness is mine," and delights in the base of infinite consciousness.
For what reason?
Because it has not been fully understood by him, I say.
He perceives the base of nothingness as the base of nothingness.
Having perceived the base of nothingness as the base of nothingness, one conceives the base of nothingness, conceives in the base of nothingness,
conceives from the base of nothingness, conceives "the base of nothingness is mine," and delights in the base of nothingness.
For what reason?
‘It is not fully understood by him,’ I say.
One perceives the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception as the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception;
having perceived the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception as the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, one [regards] the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception...

One conceives [in relation] to the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception; one conceives from the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception; one conceives, "The base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception is mine";
one delights in the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception.
For what reason?
‘That has not been fully understood by him,’ I say.
One perceives what is seen as ‘seen’;
having perceived what is seen as ‘seen,’ one conceives of the seen, one conceives in the seen, one conceives from the seen, one conceives ‘the seen is mine,’ and one delights in the seen.
And why is that? Because I say that it has not been fully understood by him.
He perceives what has been heard as merely heard.

Having perceived what has been heard as "heard," one conceives of it as heard; one conceives in regard to what is heard, one conceives from what is heard, one conceives "this is mine" regarding what is heard, and one delights in what is heard.
For what reason?
Because it has not been fully understood, I say.
One perceives the sensed as sensed.
Having perceived the sensed as sensed, one conceives of the sensed, conceives in the sensed, conceives from the sensed, conceives "the sensed is mine," and delights in the sensed.
For what reason?
“I say that this has not been fully understood by him.
One perceives what is cognized as “cognized”;

having perceived what is cognized as “cognized,” one conceives of the cognized, conceives in regard to the cognized, conceives from the cognized, conceives “the cognized is mine,” and delights in the cognized.
For what reason?
Because it has not been fully understood by him, I say.
He perceives unity as unity.
Having perceived unity as unity, one conceives of unity, conceives in unity, conceives from unity, conceives "unity is mine," and delights in unity.
For what reason?
Because it has not been fully understood by him, I say.
One perceives diversity as diversity;
having perceived diversity as diversity, one conceives of diversity, conceives in diversity, conceives from diversity, conceives "diversity is mine," and delights in diversity.
For what reason?
"I say that this has not been fully understood by him.
He perceives everything as everything;
having perceived everything as everything, he conceives of everything, he conceives in everything, he conceives from everything, he conceives, 'Everything is mine,' and he delights in everything.
And why is that? Because I say it has not been fully understood by him.
He perceives Nibbāna as Nibbāna.
Having perceived Nibbāna as Nibbāna, one conceives of Nibbāna, conceives in Nibbāna, conceives from Nibbāna, conceives "Nibbāna is mine," and delights in Nibbāna.
For what reason?
Because it has not been fully understood by him, I say.
The first section on the plane of the ordinary person (*puthujjana*) is concluded.

Furthermore, monks, even that monk who is still in training (*sekkha*), whose mind has not yet reached its goal, and who dwells aspiring for the unsurpassed security from bondage, directly knows the earth as earth;

having directly known the earth as earth, he should not conceive "earth," he should not conceive "in the earth," he should not conceive "from the earth," he should not conceive "earth is mine," and he should not delight in the earth.
And why is that? Because I say:
"It must be fully understood by him. [The same applies to] water... [and so on].
Fire ...
wind ... beings ...
To Deva...
to Pajāpati...
to Brahmā...
...the Ābhassara [deities] ...
the Subhakiṇha [deities] ...
the Vehapphala [deities] ...
The base of mastery … the base of infinite space … the base of infinite consciousness …
the base of nothingness … the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception … the seen …
the heard … the sensed … the cognized …
unity … diversity … all …
One directly knows Nibbāna as Nibbāna.

Having directly known Nibbāna as Nibbāna, one should not conceive "Nibbāna," one should not conceive "in Nibbāna," one should not conceive "from Nibbāna," one should not conceive "Nibbāna is mine," and one should not delight in Nibbāna.
For what reason?
‘It is to be fully understood by him,’ I say.
This concludes the section on the determination of the second method according to the trainee (sekha).

Furthermore, monks, even that bhikkhu who is an arahant, whose taints are destroyed, who has lived the holy life, done what was to be done, laid down the burden, attained his own goal, whose fetters of existence are utterly exhausted, and who is liberated through right gnosis—he too directly knows earth as earth.

Having directly known earth as earth, one does not conceive of earth, one does not conceive in earth, one does not conceive from earth, one does not conceive "earth is mine," and one does not delight in earth.
For what reason?
Because it has been fully understood by him, I say.
Water ...
fire ...
air ...
... the spirits ...
the gods ...
Pajāpati ...
... the Brahmā realm ...
the Ābhassara realm ...
the Subhakiṇha realm ...
... of great fruit ...
the master ...
the base of infinite space ...
the base of infinite consciousness … the base of nothingness … the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception …
The seen … the heard … the sensed …
the cognized … unity … diversity …
He directly knows all as all, suffering as suffering, origination as origination, cessation as cessation, and Nibbāna as Nibbāna.

Having directly known Nibbāna as Nibbāna, he does not conceive Nibbāna, he does not conceive in Nibbāna, he does not conceive from Nibbāna, he does not conceive "Nibbāna is mine," and he does not delight in Nibbāna.
Why is that? Because I say, "It has been fully understood by him.
The section on the third method concerning those whose taints are destroyed is finished.

"Furthermore, monks, even that monk who is an arahant, whose taints are destroyed, who has lived the holy life, done what was to be done, laid down the burden, attained his own goal, whose fetters of existence are utterly exhausted, and who is liberated through right gnosis—he too directly knows earth as earth.

Having directly known earth as earth, he does not conceive of earth, he does not conceive in earth, he does not conceive from earth, he does not conceive 'earth is mine,' and he does not delight in earth. Why is that?"
Through the destruction of lust, because of being free from lust.
[The same applies to] water...
fire... [and air].
... the wind ...
the spirits ...
the gods ...
Pajāpati … Brahmā … the Ābhassara devas …
...the Subhakiṇha realm...
the Vehapphala realm...
the Abhibhu realm...
the base of infinite space … the base of infinite consciousness … the base of nothingness …
the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception … the seen … the heard …
the sensed … the cognized … unity …
He directly knows diversity … everything … and Nibbāna as Nibbāna.

Having directly known nibbāna as nibbāna, one does not conceive of nibbāna, does not conceive in nibbāna, does not conceive from nibbāna, does not conceive "nibbāna is mine," and does not delight in nibbāna.
For what reason?
Because of the destruction of lust, due to being free from lust.
The section on the fourth method, concerning those whose taints are destroyed, is finished.

Furthermore, monks, that monk who is an arahant, whose taints are destroyed, who has lived the holy life, done what was to be done, laid down the burden, attained his own goal, whose fetters of existence are utterly exhausted, and who is liberated through right gnosis—he too directly knows earth as earth;

having directly known earth as earth, he does not conceive earth, he does not conceive [himself] in earth, he does not conceive [himself] from earth, he does not conceive "earth is mine," and he does not delight in earth.
For what reason?
Because of the destruction of hatred and because of being free from hatred.
[The same applies to] water... [and so forth].
fire … wind … beings …
To the devas...
to Pajāpati...
to Brahmā...
...the Ābhassara [deities] ...
the Subhakiṇha [deities] ...
the Vehapphala [deities] ...
The base of mastery … the base of infinite space … the base of infinite consciousness …
the base of nothingness … the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception … the seen …
the heard … the sensed … the cognized …
Unity … diversity … everything …
One directly knows Nibbāna as Nibbāna.

Having directly known Nibbāna as Nibbāna, one does not conceive of Nibbāna, one does not conceive in Nibbāna, one does not conceive from Nibbāna, one does not conceive "Nibbāna is mine," and one does not delight in Nibbāna.
For what reason?
Through the destruction of hatred, because he is free from hatred.
The fifth section on the stages of the method, by way of the destruction of the taints (*khīṇāsava*), is finished.

Furthermore, monks, that monk who is an *arahant*, whose taints are destroyed, who has lived the holy life, done what was to be done, laid down the burden, attained his own goal, whose fetters of existence are utterly exhausted, and who is liberated through right gnosis—he too directly knows the earth as earth.

Having directly known earth as earth, one does not conceive of earth, one does not conceive in earth, one does not conceive from earth, one does not conceive "earth is mine," and one does not delight in earth.
For what reason? Because of the destruction of delusion; because one is free from delusion.
Water … fire … air …
... to the spirits ...
to the gods ...
to Pajāpati ...
... the Brahmā world ...
the Ābhassara world ...
the Subhakiṇha world ...
...of great fruit ...
the master ...
the base of infinite space ...
the base of infinite consciousness … the base of nothingness … the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception …
The seen … the heard … the sensed …
the cognized … unity … diversity …
He directly knows all as all; he directly knows Nibbāna as Nibbāna.

Having directly known Nibbāna as Nibbāna, he does not conceive Nibbāna, he does not conceive in Nibbāna, he does not conceive from Nibbāna, he does not conceive "Nibbāna is mine," and he does not delight in Nibbāna.
For what reason?
Because of the destruction of delusion, due to being free from delusion.
With this, the section on the sixth method by way of the one whose taints are destroyed is completed.
“Monks, the Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, directly knows the earth as earth.

Having directly known the earth as earth, he does not conceive of the earth, he does not conceive in the earth, he does not conceive from the earth, he does not conceive ‘the earth is mine,’ and he does not delight in the earth. Why is that?
Because he has understood it as it really is with right wisdom.”
“I say that for the Tathāgata, the end of full understanding has been reached,” regarding water … and fire … [and air].
... the wind ...
the spirits ...
the gods ...
... Pajāpati ...
Brahmā ...
the Ābhassara [deities] ...
...the Subhakiṇha realm...
the Vehapphala realm...
the Abhibhū realm...
the base of infinite space … the base of infinite consciousness … the base of nothingness …
The base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception … what is seen … what is heard …
the cognized … the known … unity …
He directly knows diversity ... everything ... and Nibbāna as Nibbāna.

Having directly known nibbāna as nibbāna, he does not conceive of nibbāna, he does not conceive in nibbāna, he does not conceive from nibbāna, he does not conceive, ‘Nibbāna is mine,’ and he does not delight in nibbāna.
For what reason?
“Because it has been fully understood by the Tathāgata,” I say.
The seventh chapter on the method of the Tathāgata is concluded.
Furthermore, monks, the Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Self-Awakened One, directly knows earth as earth;

having directly known earth as earth, he does not conceive of earth, he does not conceive in earth, he does not conceive from earth, he does not conceive "earth is mine," and he does not delight in earth.
And why is that? Because it has been understood: "Delight is the root of suffering," and "From becoming comes birth; for one who has come into being, there is aging and death."

"Therefore, monks, I say that it is because of the complete destruction, fading away, cessation, relinquishment, and abandonment of all cravings that the Tathāgata has awakened to unsurpassed perfect enlightenment.
[The same applies to] water...
fire..."
... the wind ...
the spirits ...
the gods ...
Pajāpati … Brahmā … the Ābhassara devas …
... the Subhakiṇha [deities] ...
the Vehapphala [deities] ...
the Abhibhus ...
the base of infinite space … the base of infinite consciousness … the base of nothingness …
the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception … the seen … the heard …
The sensed … the cognized … unity …
He directly knows diversity … all … and Nibbāna as Nibbāna.

Having directly known Nibbāna as Nibbāna, one does not conceive of Nibbāna, one does not conceive in Nibbāna, one does not conceive from Nibbāna, one does not conceive "Nibbāna is mine," and one does not delight in Nibbāna.
For what reason?
Because "delight is the root of suffering."
“Having understood thus: ‘For one who has come into being, there is birth;

for one who has been born, there is aging and death,’ therefore, monks, I say: ‘The Tathāgata, through the complete destruction, fading away, cessation, relinquishment, and renunciation of all cravings, has awakened to unsurpassed perfect enlightenment.
Thus ends the eighth section on the stages of the method concerning the Tathāgata.
Thus spoke the Blessed One.
Those monks did not delight in the Blessed One’s words.
The First Discourse on the Root Exposition is finished.
